description: Start from Eliahou's 64-modular order-668 matrix rather than from random +/-1 matrices. Encode each nonzero off-diagonal Gram entry as a defect particle on a row-pair graph and let a cellular automaton move, merge, and annihilate defects while an exact verifier stays outside the CA loop.
mathematical_formalization: Given H in {+1,-1}^{668 x 668}, define D_ij = <H_i, H_j> for i != j. Initialize from a sparse-defect seed H^(0) and apply local balanced flips U_f so that H^(t+1) = U_f(H^(t)) while E(H) = sum_{i<j} |D_ij| or sum_{i<j} D_ij^2 decreases and block invariants are preserved.
analogical_connections: Reaction-diffusion CA on a sparse defect gas.
Topological-code syndrome annihilation translated into Gram-space.
Metastable spin system lifted from a near-ground-state seed.
implementation_hypothesis: Reconstruct the published 64-modular seed, build a defect graph over row pairs, and implement local row-block sign swaps that preserve balance. Use CA rules to route defect mass toward cancellation and compare against greedy and annealed updates on the same neighborhood.
experiment_seed: Validate on smaller exact Hadamards with injected defects, then start from the 668 modular seed and measure defect count, defect energy, and exact-certificate frequency after fixed update budgets.

closest_prior_art.title: Finding a Hadamard Matrix by Simulated Annealing of Spin-Vectors
Cellular-automaton decoders for topological quantum memories

novelty_claim: The new element is not 'CA for search' in general, but CA as a Hadamard-specific defect-repair layer initialized from the published 64-modular 668 seed.
differentiation: Prior Hadamard heuristics optimize directly in matrix or sequence coordinates, while prior CA decoders repair stabilizer syndromes. This concept combines the two only at the sparse residual-defect stage exposed by the best current 668 construction.
